data.gender_notes: Liviah is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Greek, Liviah means 'God is my life'. It is a biblical name, as it appears in the Old Testament in the book of Ezra. The name Liviah carries the meaning “God is my life” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Liviah usually hope their child will grow to embody god is my life and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A reminder of the divine presence in one's life.
data.etymology: Liviah belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “God is my life.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Liviah total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: The name Liviah carries a strong and profound message of faith and trust in God. It resonates with the belief that God is the source of life and sustenance, and that He is an integral part of our existence. This belief is a core tenet of Christianity and is freely expressed through the name.
data.spiritual_significance: Liviah is a powerful name from a spiritual perspective, as it symbolizes a deep connection with God. It reflects the belief that God is not just the creator of life but is also intimately involved in every aspect of our lives. It is a reminder that our lives are not our own but are gifts from God, and that we should live in a way that honors and glorifies Him. Additionally, the name Liviah may serve as a source of strength and comfort for those facing difficult times, as it reinforces the belief that God is present and active in their lives.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Liviah is a Hebrew name meaning "Living," symbolizing the vibrant, dynamic, and abundant life that comes from being deeply connected to God. It is a reminder of the eternal and spiritual nature of our souls, urging us to live fully and faithfully in the present moment.
